description:
## Why

Wire AIA URL extraction (PKIX-a1yc.3) + OCSP request building (PKIX-a1yc.4) + RevocationFetcher (PKIX-a1yc.1) + pkix-revocation::OcspChecker into a single RevocationChecker that POSTs OCSP queries to the responder URL extracted from the cert's AIA extension.

## What

Replace the placeholder `HttpOcspFetcher<F>` with a working impl:

```rust
#[cfg(feature = "ocsp")]
pub struct HttpOcspFetcher<F, V> {
    fetcher: F,
    verifier: V,
    now_unix: u64,
    hash_alg: OcspHashAlg, // configurable; default SHA-256
}

#[cfg(feature = "ocsp")]
impl<F: RevocationFetcher, V: SignatureVerifier + Clone> HttpOcspFetcher<F, V> {
    pub const fn new(fetcher: F, verifier: V, now_unix: u64) -> Self;
    pub const fn with_hash_alg(self, alg: OcspHashAlg) -> Self;
}

#[cfg(feature = "ocsp")]
impl<F: RevocationFetcher, V: SignatureVerifier + Clone> RevocationChecker
    for HttpOcspFetcher<F, V>
{
    fn check_revocation(&self, cert: &Certificate, issuer: &Certificate)
        -> pkix_revocation::Result<()>;

    fn check_revocation_against_anchor(...) -> ...;
}
```

### check_revocation flow

1. Extract AIA OCSP URLs from cert (via PKIX-a1yc.3 helper). If empty, return Ok(()) — no OCSP responder means no OCSP-based status; document.
2. Build OCSP request DER bytes via PKIX-a1yc.4 helper using cert + issuer + hash_alg. On build error, surface it.
3. For each URL in order:
   a. `fetcher.fetch(POST, url, body=request_bytes, content_type="application/ocsp-request")`. On error, continue to next URL.
   b. Optional content-type sanity check on response (warn but accept if missing — many responders are loose).
   c. `OcspChecker::new(response_bytes, now_unix, verifier.clone())` → if OCSPResponse status != successful or parse fails, continue to next URL.
   d. `checker.check_revocation(cert, issuer)` → return result.
4. If all URLs fail, surface a clear error.

### check_revocation_against_anchor flow

Identical, with issuer = anchor.cert. Document and test that an OCSP response signed by the trust anchor itself is acceptable.

## Acceptance

- [ ] HttpOcspFetcher impls RevocationChecker (and against_anchor).
- [ ] Empty AIA list returns Ok(()) (documented).
- [ ] First successful POST+parse path taken.
- [ ] Configurable hash algorithm (SHA-1 / SHA-256).
- [ ] Tests with mock RevocationFetcher (canned response bytes) covering: cert revoked, cert good, cert unknown, fetcher all-fail, malformed response on first URL falls back to second.
- [ ] No new pkix-revocation deps.

## Out of scope

- Caching (PKIX-a1yc.7).
- Nonce verification.
- Delegated OCSP responder cert chain validation (separate bead — for v0.x the OCSP signature must verify with the cert's issuer key directly OR with a delegated responder cert that x509-ocsp's BasicOcspResponse can pull in via certs[]; behaviour is whatever pkix-revocation::OcspChecker already does).
- Stapled OCSP (TLS concern, out of scope for whole crate).

## Effort

~200 lines + tests.

## Depends on

PKIX-a1yc.1, PKIX-a1yc.3, PKIX-a1yc.4.
